method: All five source files read completely; Git blob and SHA256 verified. Upstream tests not run.
findings: Symlink tests distinguish link text from regular-file bytes, cover follow/ignore/see modes and original flags, and ensure ignored broken symlinks do not prevent directory matching. Default-path-set test does not assert record types.

stdin tests use subprocess argument arrays and cover newline-separated names, NUL-separated names containing newlines, leading-dash paths after --, and empty stdin without implicit current-directory traversal. These subprocesses use communicate without timeout and do not assert returncode.

Hardlink tests explicitly assert original flags for no-hardlinked, hardlinked and keep-hardlinked plus tagged roots. Initial single-group tests index expected records but do not assert total record count; multiple-original tests do assert counts.

Repeated-path tests cover identical roots, direct files, overlapping directory/file inputs, symlink aliases and directory loops. Most assertions only count duplicate_file records, so unrelated record types are not rejected. Bind-mount test requires root and explicitly checks final record count and ordering.
Broken-symlink-as-argument regression checks exactly two badlink records and both full paths.

Our existing exact tests separate hardlink aliases from independently copied bytes and test followed symlink cycles. Their semantics concern physical-file deduplication rather than rmlint original-selection policies.
limits: No bind mounts or generated deletion scripts executed.
No performance improvement claimed; repository review remains partial.

local_verification.scope: Current host filesystem; default and followed symlinks, directory cycle, repeated direct input, physical aliases versus independent copy. No bind-mount or Windows runtime coverage.
